text:
maya: Heads up — after merging the candidate-normalizer PR (abc1234) I'm seeing an oddity: NDCG@10 down ~2.4% on rankbench dev but MRR@10 slightly up. Anyone else?
kevin: USR: ran a quick spot-check. The PR touched doc-side whitespace/emoji normalizer and the tokenizer mapping. Might be token boundary shifts.
priya: Running the standard parity script now. Quick command I used: `./bin/rankbench --model ranklight-v3 --split dev --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42`
priya: Past run (before PR):
```
ndcg@10: 0.4123
mrr@10: 0.2431
```
priya: New run (after PR):
```
ndcg@10: 0.4033
mrr@10: 0.2450
```
kevin: Interesting — NDCG drop mostly on long-doc cohorts. Short-queries seem stable. I diffed token counts: median doc token len decreased by ~6 tokens after normalization.
tony: Could shorter tokenization be collapsing topical context, harming ranking order (NDCG) but boosting top-1 precision (MRR) for some queries?
maya: That matches what I saw in candidate-level deltas: head items moved up for a subset of queries. We should check whether normalization changed punctuation joins (e.g., turning `end...` into `end.`) which affects suffix matching.
kevin: FYI I ran tokenizer parity: `python -c "import tok; print(tok.stats('before'), tok.stats('after'))"` — differences in "+zero-width" handling and emoji splitting are non-trivial.
priya: Also noticed the eval harness strips HTML differently now; some candidate snippets lose sentence boundaries, causing shorter passages. Adding this to checklist.
eval-bot: automatic-run: rankbench ablation scheduled (run-id: rb-174888). Tests queued: normalization=on/off, tokenizer=before/after, quant=fp16/int4. ETA ~30m. :gear:
maya: Can we prioritize ablation on the real holdout (not dev)? We need to make sure it's not a dev-only fluke.
priya: yep queued holdout run as well. linking results when done.
tony: If it's indeed normalization-induced, simplest rollback is to revert the doc-side joiner change and keep candidate normalizer. But we should try targeted ablation: only revert emoji joiner.
kevin: Also wondering if quantization (we're testing int4 rollouts soon) amplifies this effect. Shorter token sequences change KV cache behavior and might interact with per-layer quant scaling. Recommend running quantized eval with both normalizers.
maya: Agreed. Action items: 1) Wait for eval-bot results. 2) Run parity diff on seqlen and punctuation tokens (kevin). 3) Re-run candidate-level deltas on holdout (priya). 4) If replicated, plan a small revert PR for doc-joiner and run canary.
priya: I'll post RMSE of score deltas per-query and a small csv of affected query ids once runs finish.
eval-bot: results: ablation finished. summary:
```
normalizer=on tokenizer=after quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4033 mrr@10 0.2450
normalizer=off tokenizer=after quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4121 mrr@10 0.2432
normalizer=on tokenizer=before quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4118 mrr@10 0.2430
normalizer=on tokenizer=after quant=int4  -> ndcg@10 0.3999 mrr@10 0.2462
```
kevin: That table suggests tokenizer change plus normalizer is the culprit; tokenizer-before preserves ndcg. int4 worsens ndcg slightly when normalizer+tokenizer-after used.
tony: So root cause: new tokenizer mapping + normalizer interaction. Plan: revert tokenizer mapping for doc-side joiners and keep candidate-normalizer. Then run canary on dedicated bucket.
maya: Sounds good. I'll open the rollback PR and tag you all. Please add any extra probes to the canary checklist (esp. long-doc cohorts).
priya: tagging existing alerts for ndcg regression so we don't auto-promote. :warning:
kevin: I'll include a small script to produce token-level diffs for the canary so SRE/product can inspect.
maya: Thanks — will follow up with rollout plan after canary results.
